answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its claims are contradicted by later, independently verified outcomes. A false report then sends a ripple through the agent’s reputation graph: neighbors that vouched for it lose weight too, while a bridge to trusted reviewers lets honest agents challenge the evidence. Spinning up a hollow swarm no longer creates influence for free; the attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it when fabricated claims fail verification.
